task: T27 item 4 — visibility catch-up (M4 skip-not-queue) + item 5 wall-clock catch-up
method: From the page, paused the live interval, temporarily wrapped scheduler._emitTick with a counter (instrumentation removed after the test), rewound epochStartTime by ~12s of simulated wall-clock, then dispatched a single onVisibilityChange() while the page is visible. Asserted exactly ONE emit and a single forward jump to the wall-clock target tick (no burst replay of intervening ticks).

handler_wiring.note: scheduler._visibilityHandler is a live function bound via document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', ...). The real tab-background -> foreground transition therefore routes through onVisibilityChange(), which computes targetTick = floor((performance.now()-epochStartTime)/1000) % epochLength and emits once.
handler_wiring.hidden_guard: onVisibilityChange() early-returns when document.visibilityState === 'hidden' (and when _paused / _inEpochReset), so no tick fires while backgrounded — only the single forward catch-up on return to foreground.

item5_tab_background_raf_pause.nature: browser-native (RAF auto-pauses in background tabs); tick advance uses setInterval(1000ms) + performance.now() epochStartTime, never RAF, so simulation time is reconciled from wall clock on return.
item5_tab_background_raf_pause.verified: wall-clock catch-up = the single-jump result above (tick reconciled to elapsed wall time in one emit).

instrumentation_cleanup: scheduler._emitTick restored to original; __emitLog/__origEmit deleted; scheduler stop()+reset to epochLength=180 after test.
verdict: PASS — single skip-not-queue jump to the wall-clock target tick, no tick avalanche; visibilitychange handler is wired for the native background/foreground path.
